basis: Cranioacral malformations and contractures with congenital septal and pulmonary-valve defects form the reported syndrome; cardiac frequency is unquantified.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: inferred core congenital cardiac component (VSD/pulmonic stenosis), alongside cranioacral abnormalities; frequency is unquantified.

basis: Lysosomal free sialic acid storage disorder defined by severe neurodevelopmental impairment and progressive CNS dysfunction.

decisions.neurologic: primary: neurodegeneration defines this severity subtype, rather than an optional complication ([GeneReviews](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK1470/)).

basis: Short-rib skeletal dysplasia; pulmonary hypoplasia with respiratory impairment is a major clinical feature. Common renal injury is not established for IFT80 disease.

decisions.pulmonary: involved: pulmonary hypoplasia causes respiratory impairment, a major feature of asphyxiating thoracic dystrophy; thoracic skeletal dysplasia is primary.

basis: Axonal neuropathy from disordered sphingolipid biosynthesis; muscle wasting reflects denervation. Singleton cataract does not establish common ocular disease.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: muscle atrophy/weakness reflects motor denervation, not direct muscle disease; the 1/1 observation does not establish common intrinsic myopathy.

basis: PAH metabolic deficiency spans benign hyperphenylalaninemia through PKU; common neurologic injury across the entire spectrum is not established.

decisions.neurologic: none: untreated PKU can injure the brain, but this umbrella includes benign mild hyperphenylalaninemia; persistent neurologic injury at >=30% across the spectrum is not established.

basis: Joint hypermobility 21/29 and vertebral changes 30-79%; progressive visual loss 30-79%; cardiac defects/HTN 30-79% omitted by cap. Lisch nodules alone are non-damaging.

decisions.cardiovascular: none under cap: cardiac abnormalities and hypertension are reported in 30-79%; retain more frequent skeletal abnormalities and progressive visual loss with explicit functional damage.
decisions.ocular: involved: progressive visual loss is reported in 30-79%, establishing functional eye damage; Lisch nodules alone would not qualify.

basis: ETFB-related fatty-acid/amino-acid oxidation disorder; muscle injury frequency is unestablished for this genetic subtype, so pooled MADD myopathy rates are insufficient.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: ETFB-specific myopathy >=30% is unestablished; late-onset MADD rates cannot be assumed ([GeneReviews](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK558236/)).

basis: Cerebellar developmental disease; nystagmus and pursuit abnormalities are central motor signs. Frequent strabismus does not establish intrinsic ocular injury.

decisions.ocular: none: strabismus occurs in 30-79%, but the evidence supports cerebellar ocular-motor dysfunction without direct eye damage or established visual loss.

basis: Corneal fragility defines disease; joint abnormalities occur in 80-99% and hearing loss in 30-79%. These are extraocular involvement; skin laxity alone does not establish injury.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: joint connective-tissue abnormalities occur in 80-99%; they are extraocular manifestations accompanying the defining corneal disease.

basis: Storage disease defined by hepatic injury and neurodegeneration; lung infiltration 80-99%, respiratory failure 30-79%. Splenic/blood involvement omitted by cap; cherry-red spots alone do not qualify.

decisions.hepatic: primary: hepatosplenomegaly is defining, with hepatomegaly and elevated transaminases in 10/10; liver failure occurs in 30-79%.
decisions.neurologic: primary: rapidly progressive neurodegeneration defines type A; developmental regression/delay occurs in 10/10, not merely as an optional complication.
